{"filepath": "satisfactory_planner/gui/main_window.py", "search": "    def _refresh_recipe_list(self):
        self.recipe_list.clear()
        for recipe in self.recipe_registry.all_recipes():
            item = QListWidgetItem(recipe.name)
            item.setData(Qt.ItemDataRole.UserRole, recipe.name)
            self.recipe_list.addItem(item)
        
        # Update available items for target selection
        self._update_available_items()", "replace": "    def _refresh_recipe_list(self):
        # Block signals to avoid triggering itemChanged during refresh
        self.recipe_list.blockSignals(True)
        self.recipe_list.clear()
        for recipe in self.recipe_registry.all_recipes():
            item = QListWidgetItem(recipe.name)
            item.setData(Qt.ItemDataRole.UserRole, recipe.name)
            item.setFlags(item.flags() | Qt.ItemFlag.ItemIsUserCheckable)
            # Checked = enabled, unchecked = disabled
            if self.recipe_registry.is_disabled(recipe.name):
                item.setCheckState(Qt.CheckState.Unchecked)
            else:
                item.setCheckState(Qt.CheckState.Checked)
            self.recipe_list.addItem(item)
        self.recipe_list.blockSignals(False)
        
        # Update available items for target selection
        self._update_available_items()"}

I've implemented the recipe disable/enable feature. Here's what was added:

## Changes Made

### 1. RecipeRegistry (models/recipe.py)
- Added `_disabled: set[str]` to track disabled recipe names
- New methods: `is_disabled()`, `set_disabled()`, `enabled_recipes()`, `disabled_recipe_names()`
- Cleans up disabled set when loading recipes (removes stale entries)

### 2. calculate_requirements (algorithms/requirements.py)
- Added `disabled_recipes: Optional[set[str]]` parameter
- Filters out disabled recipes when searching for recipes that produce an item

### 3. MainWindow (gui/main_window.py)
- Added `get_disabled_recipes_path()` → `~/.local/share/satisfactory-planner/disabled_recipes.json`
- Recipe list items now have checkboxes (checked = enabled, unchecked = disabled)
- Connected `itemChanged` signal to toggle disabled state
- Loads disabled recipes on startup, saves on close
- Passes disabled recipes to `calculate_requirements()`

## How it works
- Each recipe in the list now shows a checkbox
- Unchecking a recipe disables it (grays out the checkbox)
- Disabled recipes are ignored when calculating production requirements
- The disabled state persists across sessions via XDG data directory
